transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

My regular doctor sent me. She says my weight has gotten too low, and everyone’s been making a big fuss about it. I don’t really see it the same way, though. Being lighter feels like it helps me keep moving at the shop and not get slowed down.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?

Yes. I mean… I don’t like saying it that way, but yes. If I eat something heavy, or those holiday foods we used to make, I start worrying right away that I’ll gain weight and lose the control I’ve worked so hard to keep.
Do you ever eat a large amount of food in a short period of time?
I’m not sure. I don’t think of it that way. I mostly notice what I’m eating and try to keep it under control, so “a large amount” is hard for me to judge.
Do you ever feel like you've lost control while eating?
I don’t know if I’d call it losing control. Usually I’m pretty aware of what I’m eating. Sometimes I feel anxious afterward, but during it… I’m not sure that I lose control exactly.
Do you ever make yourself vomit after eating?
I don’t really know how to answer that. I mean, I’ve felt bad after eating, but I’m not sure about making myself vomit. I haven’t really thought of it that way.
Have you ever made yourself vomit after eating?
I’m not sure. I don’t really think I’ve made myself vomit, no. I’ve felt upset after eating, but I don’t know that I’ve done that on purpose.
Do you ever exercise excessively to try to burn off calories after eating?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I do try to stay active, but I don’t know that I’d call it excessive or specifically to burn off food.
Do you ever eat much more quickly than normal when you're eating?
I haven’t really noticed that, no. I don’t think I eat especially fast.
Is your fear of gaining weight one of the main things that motivates you to control your eating?

Yes. If I eat anything that feels too heavy, or foods like we used to make for holidays, I start worrying right away that I’m going to gain weight. It feels like I’ll lose the control I’ve worked really hard to keep.
Do you ever use laxatives or diuretics to try to control your weight?
No, I don’t use laxatives or water pills for that. That’s not something I do.
Do you think your weight is currently too low?
No, I don’t think it’s too low. My husband says I look too thin, and even the apprentices at work have said things, but I think they’re mixing up discipline with being sick. I feel like I’m fine.
Do you think you look too thin?
No, I don’t really see myself that way. My husband says I look too thin, and some of the apprentices have said it too, but I tell them I’m fine. I think they’re confusing discipline with being sick.
Do you think your weight is normal for your height?

I think it’s normal, yes. I mean, my husband and the apprentices keep saying I look too thin, but I don’t see it that way. I tell them I’m fine — I think people are confusing discipline with being sick.
Do you ever feel like you've eaten an amount of food that is much larger than what most people would eat in a similar time period?
No, I don’t think so. I don’t really have times where I feel like I’ve eaten some unusually large amount compared to other people.
Have you been intentionally restricting the amount of food you eat to avoid gaining weight?

I suppose I do keep it pretty limited, yes. On workshop days I’ll usually just have tea, maybe a few careful bites of something. Stopping for a real meal feels unnecessary to me, and it kind of throws off the control I’ve got over the day.
Do you think your body shape or weight is the way you want it to be?

Mostly, yes. I know my doctor sent me here because my weight has gotten so low and everyone’s making a fuss about it, but I don’t really see it as a problem. Being this light feels like it helps me keep moving in the shop and not get slowed down.
Do you ever feel like you've eaten an amount of food that is more than you planned to eat?
Not really. I usually know what I’m going to eat ahead of time, and I don’t often go past that. If anything, I’m more likely to stop short than eat more than I meant to.
Do you think there's anything wrong with your body shape?
I don’t think so, no. My husband and the apprentices say I look too thin, but I think they’re making too much of it. To me, it’s discipline, not sickness.
Do you think your weight or body shape is the main thing that determines your self-worth?
I’m not sure I’d put it that way. I do feel better about myself when I’m keeping my weight where I want it, but I don’t know if it’s the main thing. Work and being useful matter a lot to me too.
Have you had your menstrual period in the past few months?
No, I haven’t—though at my age I wouldn’t expect to.
